text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to determine the cause, do you have any history of kidney stones, fever, or recent trauma? Also, does the pain radiate toward your groin?

text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections, have you experienced any fever, chills, or nausea along with the current pain? Additionally, have you noticed any painless episodes of blood in your urine in the past, or is this your first occurrence?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Ureterolithiasis (Kidney Stone)
